lines.text: Lead with Sydney, then Toronto and New York: that is where the comparable books' readers are strongest of the markets checked.
Aim the launch at people aged 24 and under, as planned.
Name the genre, motivation, and the closest comparable book in the first line of the blurb and of the pitch to booksellers.
Lead the key messages with resilience, mental toughness and overcoming adversity, the themes the comparable books share.

Pitch the book to booksellers, press and readers in the company of Atomic Habits: An Easy & Proven Way to Build Good Habits & Break Bad Ones, The Way of the Superior Man: A Spiritual Guide to Mastering the Challenges of Women, Work, and Sexual Desire and Can't Hurt Me: Master Your Mind and Defy the Odds.

lines.text: The core readers are people 24 and under, then 35 to 44.
They also hear Fresh Air and Curious Minds at Work.
Among the markets a launch like this usually checks, the comparable books' readers is strongest in Sydney, then Toronto, New York, London and Lagos.
Put the two closest comparable books in the first line of the pitch to booksellers and in the note to reviewers.
For audio, offer the author to Fresh Air and Curious Minds at Work, the podcasts your readers hear.
Use these as comparisons in the pitch only. Do not announce an adaptation until a producer is attached.
Open pre-orders on every retail page eight weeks out, and ask the buyers for a display or a promotion slot against the closest comparable book.
Ask Word On The Water - The London Bookbarge and Hatchards in London to stock and display the book: they rank highest with your readers.

Give book clubs a reading kit and the first chapter before launch, and offer the author for one club evening in each lead market.
Hook one: open on the strongest image of How to be a man in the first two seconds.
Hook two: open on the question this release answers, as text on screen over the first shot.

Key art brief: one image, the title How to be a man and at most one line of text. Say what the image must show, what to avoid and where it will be seen, then hand it to a designer. Oraqul writes the brief; a person makes the art.
